clue.text: Superior types go after dope

indicators.note: after places the word for go behind the word for dope

parts.note: dope is slang for information, as is gen
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Snobs take a shot only once they have the inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the landed upper class, people of superior social rank.

clue.text: Joy, to finish up in a quantity of drink

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the drink

parts.note: a glass is a measure of drink

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for finish is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to finish is to end

explanation.surface: Happiness, so the speaker says, means draining the last of one's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish up' reads like draining a glass, but 'up' only signals that the word for finish runs upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is a synonym of joy, a feeling of happiness.

clue.text: Fruit aren't nice when rot ten

indicators.note: split into two words, rot ten tells us these letters have gone bad and need reworking

explanation.surface: A complaint that fruit stops being pleasant once it has gone rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rot ten' is the word rotten split in two, so it reads as a misprint while serving as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach, a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Status is absolute

definitions.meaning: standing or position in a hierarchy

explanation.definitionFit: Rank means one's grade or standing, and as an adjective means utter, total.

clue.text: Bill is extra cover in the rain

definitions.meaning: a second outer sheet stretched over a tent to keep rain off

explanation.surface: A notice says an extra layer is needed when it pours.
explanation.definitionFit: A flysheet is both a single printed leaflet and the outer waterproof sheet over a tent.

clue.text: Window space in vault sealant kept clear

indicators.note: kept means the sealant word holds the second piece inside it

parts.note: lute is a clay or cement used to seal joints
clear in the sense of after deductions, like net profit

explanation.surface: A builder notes that the arched window was sealed and kept clear.
explanation.walkthrough: LUTE, a sealing clay, holds NET to give LU-NET-TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is a crescent or half-moon shaped opening or window in a vaulted ceiling.

clue.text: Not a sound form of screening from the last century

definitions.text: Not a sound form of screening from the last century

parts.words: Not a sound form of screening from the last century
parts.note: sounds like a dubious way to screen something, but means a kind of movie with no soundtrack, made in the twentieth century

explanation.definitionFit: Early cinema without recorded dialogue was shown in the early twentieth century, silent with captions.

clue.text: Trimmed and was commonly evasive

definitions.meaning: hedged, said with the H dropped as in Cockney speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' signals the dropped H of informal London speech: 'hedged' becomes 'edged'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edged means bordered or trimmed, and with a dropped H it sounds like hedged, avoided committing.

clue.text: Losing energy, I call "Time" first

indicators.note: first places the time abbreviation at the front

parts.note: to ring is to telephone or call

explanation.surface: A tired barman calls last orders early.
explanation.walkthrough: "Time" is what a British pub landlord calls at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiring describes something that wears you out, draining your strength.

clue.text: Dance a short time, raising foot a little

indicators.note: in a down entry, the foot letters move up one place, so the bottom pair swap

parts.note: a minute is a short time

explanation.surface: A dancer pauses briefly, lifting a foot slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: In MINUTE the T at the foot moves up past the E, giving MINUET.
explanation.definitionFit: The minuet is a stately seventeenth-century ballroom dance in triple time.

clue.text: Rise of Atlantic island

definitions.meaning: a small British island in the South Atlantic

explanation.definitionFit: Ascension means rising up, and Ascension Island lies in the South Atlantic.

clue.text: Having proper turn, swallow good drink

indicators.note: swallow means the turned word takes the good letter inside it
turn means the word for proper is read backwards

parts.note: real means genuine or proper

explanation.surface: A drinker, having taken a proper turn, gulps down a decent drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes LAER from REAL, and 'swallow' takes G inside it: LA-G-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a pale beer, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Trap to catch a cow

indicators.note: to catch means the trap word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A farmer sets a snare to capture a cow.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an old word for cattle, so a single neat is an ox or cow.

clue.text: The county for the sporting fellow

parts.note: hunting is a field sport
a don is a college fellow

explanation.surface: A rural county suited to a man keen on field sports.
explanation.walkthrough: Huntingdon was the county town of Huntingdonshire, an old English county, often called simply Huntingdon.
explanation.definitionFit: Huntingdon(shire) is an old county of eastern England.

clue.text: Stopped trading in unionised factory

definitions.meaning: read literally, a store that has shut its doors
a workplace where all staff must belong to a trade union

explanation.surface: A works that has stopped production because of a union dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed shop is a workplace requiring union membership, and literally a store shut for business.

clue.text: Pan ready to hold what sportsman's bagged

indicators.note: to hold means the word for ready contains the next piece

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
a hunter's bag of game is the kill

explanation.surface: A pan is ready to cook the game the hunter shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A skillet is a frying pan.

clue.text: Application for getting into English newspaper

indicators.note: getting into means the word for goes inside the newspaper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A job applicant tries to get onto the staff of a national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Application means diligent effort, hard work put into a task.

clue.text: Telling off pair I sent into custody

indicators.note: sent into means the pieces are put inside the custody word

parts.note: being on remand is being held in custody

explanation.surface: A couple are given a dressing-down before being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprimand is a formal rebuke or scolding.

clue.text: Dirty business in The Wild Duck, say?

indicators.note: say means we use how the phrase is spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: Ibsen's The Wild Duck is a stage drama about a bird, so a fowl play

explanation.surface: Something shady happening during a production of Ibsen's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul play is criminal or treacherous conduct, especially murder.

clue.text: Comprehensive survey brings sound intelligence to America

indicators.note: sound means the word is used for how it is spoken

parts.note: sense means good judgment or intelligence
US is America

explanation.surface: A thorough poll brings good sense to the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a whole population.

clue.text: This could get you into hot water in Moscow

definitions.text: This could get you into hot water in Moscow

parts.words: This could get you into hot water in Moscow
parts.note: not trouble in Russia, but a Russian urn that heats water for tea

explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian metal urn used to boil water for tea.

clue.text: Topical piece old agent sent back to state

indicators.note: to means the turned pieces are attached after the state

parts.note: CAL is an abbreviation for California

indicators.note: sent back means the old agent pair is read backwards

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A news item about a former spy being deported to his homeland.
explanation.definitionFit: A calypso is a Caribbean song, often improvised on topical events.

clue.text: Honest with detectives around

indicators.note: around means the detectives surround the joining word

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: Being open and frank when the police are near.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank, open and truthful.

clue.text: From highest point, religion hit badly

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

indicators.note: badly means the letters of hit are scrambled

explanation.surface: Faith takes a blow from the very top.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the point directly overhead, hence a peak.

clue.text: Bide moment to become typical representative

indicators.note: to become means these words change into something new

explanation.surface: Wait for the right moment to become a model figure.
explanation.definitionFit: An embodiment is a perfect example or personification of a quality.

clue.text: Left in difficult position like Samson in Gaza

indicators.note: in means the left letter goes inside the predicament word

parts.note: a bind is a predicament

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a tight spot, like the biblical strongman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the Philistines put out Samson's eyes and took him to Gaza.
explanation.definitionFit: Samson had his eyes gouged out, sightless in Gaza (Judges 16).

clue.text: Bard gives pleasure

definitions.meaning: wish or desire, as in at one's pleasure

explanation.surface: Shakespeare brings delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is Shakespeare's first name and means desire or wish.

clue.text: Each holding a fruit

indicators.note: holding means the word for each goes round the next piece

parts.note: per means each, as in a pound per person

explanation.surface: Everyone is clutching a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a fruit of the tree Pyrus.

clue.text: National flag gains hearts

indicators.note: gains means the hearts letter is added after the flag

parts.note: the yellow flag is a kind of iris
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A country's banner wins over people's affections.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish describes a person or thing of Ireland, a nationality.

clue.text: Opinion given to newspaper's answering service

parts.note: a voice is a say or opinion
the Daily Mail is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A letter of opinion sent to a paper's phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: Voicemail is a system recording phone messages when nobody answers.

clue.text: Say, camouflage explorer in capital bit of greenery

indicators.note: Say means the word is taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: to camouflage is to hide
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of Africa

explanation.surface: A disguised explorer lurks in a city park.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is a large royal park in London, the capital.

clue.text: End of working week for island servant

definitions.meaning: the last weekday in a Monday-to-... week
Robinson Crusoe's companion on his island

explanation.surface: Thank goodness the week is over for the castaway's helper.
explanation.definitionFit: Friday ends the working week, and Man Friday served Crusoe in Defoe's novel.
